text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Streaming latency p99 spike detected on /v1/stream (region: us-east-1, model: redwood-llama-13b-q4) — p99 = 4.5s (SLO 1.0s), p95 = 0.95s. Automated fallback engaged for ~6% of attaches.
TelemetryBot: Correlated: node-level interrupts and NVidia ECC correctable counters increasing for node gpu-a112 (~02:14:10 UTC). Heatmap: https://console.redwood/internal/telemetry/us-east-1/pool-7/heatmap?span=6m
Liam (oncall): I'm live. Paging SRE lead @Jin. Anyone seeing customer reports?
Jin (sre): no customer tickets yet, but mobile app performance probes show streaming stalls for a small percentage of users. Rolling traces show stalled attention kernel loops with repeated memcpy retries.
Rosa (infra): pulling node metrics — gpu-a112 shows ECC_CORRECTABLE rising to 430 in 10m, fan oscillating 40-85%, and occasional thermal throttle events (throttle_count=6). NVML logs: https://console.redwood/internal/logs/gpu-a112?from=6019876530
Liam (oncall): propose immediate mitigation: 1) shift new streaming attaches away from pool-7, 2) enable model-fallback to redwood-llama-7b-quant for new streams, 3) cordon & drain gpu-a112. Agree? :eyes:
Jin (sre): agree. Prioritize minimizing new impacted sessions. Keep existent streams sticky for 20s to avoid mid-stream failovers.
Rosa (infra): applying routing change now:
```bash
redwoodctl route set --route /v1/stream --avoid-pool pool-7 --reason "live-mitigation: gpu-a112 ECC/thermal instability"
```
Rosa (infra): enabling streaming fallback policy:
```json
{"route":"/v1/stream","fallback_model":"redwood-llama-7b-quant","sticky_grace_sec":20}
```
Jin (sre): requesting detailed nvram + ECC dump and vendor diagnostics. @Hardware-Ops can you standby for RMA triage?
Hardware-Ops: on it. Please cordon node and capture dmesg, nvram, and vendor logs. I'll review and request RMA if the hardware trace confirms persistent correctables after reboot.
Rosa (infra): cordon + drain started for gpu-a112 at 6019876547. Draining active containers with graceful 20s sticky expire.
Liam (oncall): notif sent to platform-ops and customer-safety channels with brief: "Tail latency on streaming in us-east-1 due to GPU ECC/thermal instability; routing and fallback applied; investigating."
TelemetryBot: Noted a secondary signal: KV-cache miss bursts concurrent with the ECC spikes, which magnified token latency after seq_len~1024. Sample trace id: 9a3d-cc7f.
Jin (sre): debugging kernel logs inside container: repeated cudaMemcpy errors with retry backoff, attention kernel stalls observed when block-majority hits corrected ECC. Looks like kernel retries + thermal throttle = compounded tail.
Rosa (infra): scheduling a soft-reboot on gpu-a112 after drain completes (non-evacuating reboot). Command executed at 6019876550.
Hardware-Ops: post-reboot telemetry shows ECC_CORRECTABLE dropped to 4 in 3m, temps stabilized at 58C, fans 50%. However, we still see occasional micro-throttle events when sustained seq lengths >1200.
Jin (sre): p99 trending down to 1.3s after mitigation and cache prewarm, but p99 still above SLO. Initiating cache prewarm for hot prefixes to reduce KV miss tail:
```bash
redwoodctl cache prewarm --pool pool-7 --route /v1/stream --top-prefixes 250
```
Liam (oncall): estimate impact window and affected sessions?
TelemetryBot: Estimated impact window: 02:12:30 - 02:19:00 UTC; peak p99 4.5s for ~4.8 minutes. Affected streaming attaches: ~2.8% of in-flight streams, client-facing failures: 0.
Jin (sre): action items for immediate follow-up: 1) keep node cordoned until hardware ops completes extended ECC stress, 2) add per-node ECC correctable rate alert with lower threshold, 3) add automatic prewarm trigger when fallback policy activates. I'll create tickets.
Hardware-Ops: vendor diagnostic rep scheduled for next business window; we will run an overnight ECC stress test and decide on RMA tomorrow if correctables reappear. Collected vendor logs and uploaded to intel+nv support portal.
Rosa (infra): removing pool avoidance rule now that routing is stable across other pools; note: gpu-a112 remains cordoned.
Rosa (infra): command used:
```bash
redwoodctl route unset --route /v1/stream --avoid-pool pool-7
```
Liam (oncall): thanks team. I'll hand off to evening oncall @Jin in 10m. Summary for incident record (to be pasted into incident board): "Streaming tail latency spike in us-east-1 caused by ECC-correctable surge and thermal oscillation on gpu-a112. Mitigations: temporary routing avoidance, streaming-fallback to 7b quant, node cordon & soft-reboot, cache prewarm. Impact: ~2.8% streams saw p99 > SLO for ~4.8m, no request errors returned. Follow-ups: vendor stress + RMA if needed, refine alert thresholds, add automated prewarm on fallback"
Jin (sre): taking handoff at 6019876555. I'll pick up follow-ups and draft post-incident notes. :white_check_mark:
Liam (oncall): handoff acknowledged. closing live mitigation thread. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
